questions.topic: Page 9: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 9-10 Focus)
questions.questionText: Explain how the distance between two points $(x_{1}, y_{1})$ and $(x_{2}, y_{2})$ is derived using the Baudhayana-Pythagoras Theorem as shown in the textbook.

subjective_evaluation_points.point: Identify that the horizontal distance between points is $|x_{2}-x_{1}|$.
Identify that the vertical distance between points is $|y_{2}-y_{1}|$.
State that these form the two sides of a right-angled triangle with the distance between points as the hypotenuse.
Apply the theorem $c^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}$ to arrive at the formula $d = \sqrt{(x_{2}-x_{1})^{2} + (y_{2}-y_{1})^{2}}$.

questions.explanationAnswer: The derivation relies on creating a right triangle where the horizontal leg is the difference in x-coordinates and the vertical leg is the difference in y-coordinates, then using the Pythagoras theorem to find the hypotenuse.
questions.explanationQuestion: The question requires explaining the geometric derivation of the distance formula.
questions.correctAnswer: Derivation using a right triangle and Pythagoras theorem.

questions.questionText: In the experiment of pinning threads to a grid to represent a room (Fig 1.1), if the scale is $1\text{ cm} : 1\text{ foot}$, then a distance of $5\text{ cm}$ on the sketch represents a physical room distance of $5\text{ feet}$.
questions.explanationAnswer: The scale $1\text{ cm} : 1\text{ foot}$ implies a direct linear conversion where $1\text{ cm}$ on the map equals $1\text{ foot}$ in reality.
questions.explanationQuestion: The question tests the understanding of scale conversion used in the practical activity.

questions.topic: Page 9: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 9-10 Focus)
questions.questionText: If you were to map a room using pins and threads as described in the activity, why is it necessary to define an origin $(0, 0)$ and a standard scale before marking points?

subjective_evaluation_points.point: Defining an origin provides a fixed reference point to measure all other coordinates.
A standard scale ensures that the relative proportions and actual physical dimensions are maintained accurately in the sketch.

questions.explanationAnswer: The origin and scale are fundamental to creating a consistent coordinate system that allows for accurate distance and position calculation.
questions.explanationQuestion: The question requires conceptual understanding of the practical activity's requirements.
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure fixed reference and accurate dimensional representation.
